dedupe_keys.name: indigo planning tool indpt for district cooling systems

description: The INDIGO planning tool (IndPT) supports the design and assessment of district cooling systems. It was published on Zenodo by Miika Räma, Laura Sokka, Esa Pursiheimo, Krzysztof Klobut and Kati Koponen within the INDIGO project, with versions up to 2021, to help planners compare network cooling with building-specific cooling and find efficiency improvements. The tool links consumers, distribution, production and storage of cooling energy to find feasible designs of new systems, to assess the improvement potential of existing ones, and to estimate storage sizes from resource availability and variations in demand and cost. A life-cycle analysis framework evaluates economic feasibility and climate impact. Main inputs are cooling demand, the structure of cooling production, network characteristics and available resources; secondary inputs are energy prices, investments and component specifications. Coverage is not tied to a place. The tool is downloadable from Zenodo as a ZIP at no cost under a GNU General Public License. Caveats: the Zenodo licence field and the version description disagree on the GPL version, and no public source repository or documentation site was found. Simulation uses are planning district cooling networks and thermal storage, including in warming climates where cooling demand grows. Related records: model-dhnx covers heating and cooling network optimisation.
